Jeffrey Edward Gundlach is an American businessman, investor, and philanthropist. He is the founder of the investment firm DoubleLine Capital.

Daniel Seth Loeb is an American investor, hedge fund manager, and philanthropist. He is the founder and CEO of Third Point, a New York-based hedge fund focused on event-driven, value-oriented investing.

Lawrence Douglas Fink is an American businessman and the co-founder, chairman and CEO of BlackRock, a global investment management firm. His leadership spans investment management, risk analytics and the development of long-term solutions for institutional and individual investors.

John Alfred Paulson is an American hedge fund manager and the founder of Paulson & Co., established in New York in 1994. His investment career combines event-driven strategies, capital-market analysis and a focus on identifying differentiated opportunities.

William Albert Ackman is an American billionaire hedge fund manager who is the founder and chief executive officer of Pershing Square Capital Management, a hedge fund management company. His investment approach has made him an activist investor.

Tom Lee is the co-founder of Fundstrat Global Advisors and former Chief U.S. Equity Strategist at J.P. Morgan. With more than 25 years of Wall Street experience, he brings a research perspective spanning equities, macroeconomic cycles, digital assets and market structure. He co-founded Fundstrat in 2014, building an independent research platform serving institutional and individual investors. A frequent contributor to CNBC, Bloomberg and Fox Business, his approach combines macroeconomic context with quantitative and technical analysis.

LEE HUANA serves as Chief Financial Officer, with responsibility for financial strategy and the alignment of financial priorities with the division’s long-term objectives. Her background spans technology leadership, strategic analysis and scalable implementation.

Previously, she held technology leadership responsibilities at Google, including key decision-making work associated with the 2016 autonomous-driving initiative and the 2018 Google Glass project.

She holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Harvard University and earned the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charter in 2021, bringing together advanced technical expertise and professional investment knowledge.

Gerald A. Beeson is the Chief Operating Officer of Citadel. As COO, he is responsible for the firm’s key corporate functions globally and is a member of Citadel’s Portfolio Committee. Prior to becoming COO in 2008, he served as Citadel’s Chief Financial Officer. He joined Citadel in 1993 while completing his college degree and was among the company’s first employees.

Gerald received his MBA from the University of Chicago and a bachelor’s degree in Commerce with concentrations in Accountancy and Finance from DePaul University. He is registered as a certified public accountant with the State of Illinois.

Gerald is a Life Trustee and former Board Chair for DePaul University. He is also co-Chair for Big Shoulders Fund, a member of the Board of Trustees for Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, a member of the Board of Directors for Marist High School, and a member of the Civic Committee of the Commercial Club of Chicago. Gerald is a member of the 2017 Class of Henry Crown Fellows within the Aspen Global Leadership Network at the Aspen Institute.

Amanda Rubin is a senior brand strategy and corporate communications executive in the U.S. financial industry and serves as Chief Marketing Officer of Citadel and Citadel Securities. Her experience spans global financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, where she served as co-head of Global Brand and Content Strategy and participated in corporate reputation management during the financial crisis.

Since joining Citadel in 2020, she has focused on corporate brand strategy, digital communications and global talent attraction, aligning marketing with the firm’s long-term business objectives.

Recognized for her work in financial brand innovation, strategic communications and corporate influence, she was named to the Forbes 2025 Entrepreneurial CMO 50 list.

Andrew Janian is a Senior Advisor at Citadel. He previously served as the interim Chief Technology Officer where he oversaw the firm’s core technology infrastructure and directed the teams responsible for developing and operating the advanced research, investment, and risk-management platforms that power Citadel’s market-leading results across global financial markets. Previously at Citadel, he was a Senior Managing Director responsible for technology underpinning the Equities business as well as leading the firm’s Platform, Cloud and Core Engineering organizations.

Prior to joining Citadel, Andrew spent 13 years at Two Sigma, where he held a variety of senior leadership roles, including Head of Data Engineering and Chief Information Officer.

Andrew is a member of the Engineering National Council at Washington University in St. Louis and serves on the Leadership Council at Robin Hood. Previously, he served on the board of Crux Informatics and as an advisor to Uncharted Power.

Andrew received his bachelor’s degree in Computer Science from Washington University in St. Louis.

Ken Griffin is the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Citadel LLC. His leadership brings together macroeconomic research, advanced quantitative modeling and real-time risk management across global equities, fixed income, commodities and quantitative strategies. The investment platform operates at the intersection of liquidity, volatility and global capital flows through a multi-strategy framework designed to adapt across market regimes.

Shawn Fagan is Chief Legal Officer of Citadel, responsible for Citadel’s global legal, compliance, transaction management, and regulatory affairs functions. Shawn is a member of Citadel’s Portfolio Committee.

Prior to joining Citadel in 2005, Shawn was a Partner at Bartlit, Beck, Herman, Palenchar & Scott. Previously, he served as a clerk for Chief Justice William Rehnquist of the U.S. Supreme Court and Judge Douglas H. Ginsburg of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia.

Shawn serves on the Board of Directors for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Program on International Financial Systems (PIFS), is a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation (ABF), and is a member of the Economic Club of Chicago and the Legal Services Corporation’s Leaders Council.

He graduated with honors from the University of Michigan with a B.A. in Political Science and holds a J.D., magna cum laude, from Harvard Law School where he was a recipient of both the Sears Prize and John E. Thayer Award.
